transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-14 14:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Morales (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Jared Kim (Redwood SE); Aaron Cole (CTO - Harborlight), Maya Ruiz (Platform Eng), Noah Lin (Infra), Lena Park (Legal)
Shared: renewal deck (link), EU onprem tech spec (link), current usage report (shared in chat)

[00:00] Samira (Redwood): Hi everyone, thanks for hopping on, appreciate you making time. Quick roll call?
[00:10] Aaron (Harborlight): Aaron here, Maya, Noah and Lena with me.
[00:13] Maya (Harborlight): Hi, thanks.
[00:15] Samira: Great. Quick context — this is a renewal + expansion checkpoint. We have Harborlight's renewal coming up in October, and you mentioned wanting an EU on-prem top-up pilot and a bump in committed capacity. We'll run through numbers, risks, and timeline. Ethan, want to kick into the throughput side?
[00:31] Ethan (Redwood SE): Sure. So from the usage report you shared, baseline 24/7 inference is around 700 qps for the chat model across US-East, with spikes to ~1.8k qps for class of queries during batch jobs. Current Dedicated pool is nearly saturated during peak windows. If we add an EU on-prem cluster + reserved capacity we can offload steady-state and keep burst capacity in-hosted. Quick note: I may say "Redwood Dedicate" or "Reedwood Dedicate" in the notes, ignore my accent there.
[00:58] Noah (Harborlight): When you say on-prem cluster, are we talking fully air-gapped? Our compliance team prefers HSM-bound keys for PII workloads.
[01:08] Ethan: Good question. We support VPC-hosted private control plane and an on-prem package. For an EU onprem top-up pilot we can do a customer-managed control plane with K M S integration — sorry, K M S — or HSM depending on your security reqs. For HSM we have an extra onboarding step but it's supported.
[01:28] Maya: The main ask from infra is latency under 80ms p95 for inference on our EU customers. Currently routed US requests are 120-180ms p95.
[01:38] Samira: Right, that's what the EU on-prem cluster is for. If we colocate inference near the EU data stores you should see p95 drop into your target range. We'll map the exact SLO in the amendment.
[01:47] Aaron: Cost is also a constraint — we have a budget for cloud egress and dedicated nodes. We need the math on what adding EU onprem nodes does to our blended unit cost.
[01:58] Samira: Totally. We have two levers: reserved committed capacity (monthly commit for Dedicated) which lowers per-token cost, and onprem nodes which reduce cross-region egress but involve a one-time provisioning and potentially per-node infra ops fee. I'll send a blended cost scenario after this call.
[02:17] Lena (Legal): On the contract side we're primarily focused on the amendment language around data residency, audit access, and termination for failure to meet SLOs. Any standard SLAs?
[02:26] Priya (Redwood CSM): We have SLA tiers in the contract; for Dedicated we can offer a p95 latency target and uptime. If we miss SLOs we can include SLA credits. We'll get a draft amendment that includes the EU on-prem addendum and SLOs for the pilot.
[02:40] Aaron: Sounds good. Timeline? You mentioned October renewal.
[02:45] Samira: Yes, renewal window is early October. For the EU on-prem pilot we typically want provisioning 6-8 weeks before you go live. So 8 weeks from early October puts provisioning in mid-late August, which is tight, but doable if we get decisions fast.
[02:58] Maya: Ok that's tight — infra has vacations late August. Would it be possible to do a canary where we stage an initial node in a partner colo?
[03:07] Jared (Redwood): We can do a hybrid path: start with a managed co-lo deployment in EU (fast provisioning) and transition to full onprem when your infra team is ready. That reduces the critical path.
[03:18] Aaron: Hmm ok. Can you sketch the difference in lead time and cost for co-lo vs customer onprem?
[03:24] Ethan: Co-lo: ~2-3 weeks provisioning, lower initial integration work, additional egress savings but less control over HSM. Customer onprem: ~6-8 weeks, HSM/K M S integration, one-time provisioning fee. I'll put numbers in the cost scenarios.
[03:38] Noah: For the pilot we just need a small slice — say 2 nodes with 80% of the model memory quantized. Do you support quantized model variants?
[03:47] Ethan: Yes, we have quantized variants. We'll recommend a quant profile for your workload to reduce memory footprint and costs. Note — quant profiles sometimes change tokenization throughput slightly; we'll benchmark it.
[03:57] Maya: Benchmarks — can we run a real request set? Not synthetic. We can share a scrubbed dataset.
[04:04] Samira: Absolutely. Ethan, would you want Noah/Maya to share a 24-hour scrubbed trace?
[04:09] Ethan: Yes please. A scrubbed 24-hour trace with spikes highlighted and a small set of representative dialogs is best. We'll run both a latency-focused and throughput-focused benchmark. Expect results in 3-4 business days once we have the trace.
[04:22] Aaron: On encryption, will logs ever leave our VPC?
[04:26] Priya: For onprem we can keep logs within your control plane and integrate with your logging sink. In the co-lo path, certain metrics are ingested into Redwood Console for observability — can be obfuscated. We'll capture more in the security review.
[04:39] Lena: We also need a data retention policy and example audit logs for EU customers.
[04:44] Priya: I'll send our retention policy and the audit log samples in the follow-up.
[04:49] Aaron: Great.
[04:52] Samira: Shifting to capacity commit numbers — current committed throughput is X (we'll avoid exact numbers in transcript). You're looking for a step increase to cover 30% additional baseline and 50% burst headroom in EU. Is that accurate?
[05:05] Maya: Yes that's the ask. Also want staged ramp (30% for first 3 months, then evaluate).
[05:12] Samira: We can do a staged commit with optional step-ups. Pricing will reflect the staged commitment. For the renewal term, are you leaning 12 months or 24 months?
[05:23] Aaron: Our procurement prefers 12 months with an option to renew; finance is wary of multi-year locked commitments.
[05:29] Samira: Ok we'll draft a 12-month amendment with a 30/60/90 day provisioning cadence and an option for a 12-month renewal at pre-agreed rates.
[05:39] Noah: How does burst capacity work with reserved pools? If EU pool saturates, do you failover to US-hosted?
[05:46] Ethan: We do smart routing and automated fallback to compatible model variants in another region. There's a 2–5 second hedging delay depending on model and KV cache warmup. We can configure auto-fallback policies and capacity tiers; for the EU pilot we'll set a priority routing with an enforced cold-start KV policy to reduce cross-region chattiness.
[06:05] Maya: That delay is tricky — could be visible in UX. Could we have replicated KV caches in standby?
[06:12] Ethan: We can keep standby caches warmed for critical routes, but it increases resource footprint. We'll estimate cost tradeoffs in the benchmarking doc.
[06:22] Aaron: Competitor question — MajorCloudAI told us they'd host a dedicated tenant in EU for similar cost. What does Redwood bring operationally that's different?
[06:32] Samira: Two things: first, unified runtime and tooling across hosted/dedicated/on-prem — meaning your engineers don't need separate integrations. Second, cost-aware controls and observability — token-level breakdowns and quality monitoring tied to prompt sets. We also do model variant fallbacks out of the box.
[06:47] Lena: From legal POV, what indemnities around data residency?
[06:51] Priya: The standard MSA plus a EU addendum that specifies data never leaves designated regions and audit access. We'll include language in the amendment draft; your counsel can redline.
[06:59] Aaron: Ok. On the technical deep dive, will we need your SEs onsite for provisioning?
[07:04] Jared: Usually not onsite. For onprem HSM integration we run secure remote sessions and a short on-call window during provisioning. If you require an onsite engineer, that's possible but there's an extra day rate.
[07:17] Maya: Not necessary; remote is fine.
[07:20] Samira: Good. Planning calendar: if we sign amendment by 2025-09-02, provisioning in mid-Sept to mid-Oct is realistic. If sign is delayed beyond Sep 10, we risk missing early-Oct renewal alignment.
[07:34] Aaron: Procurement timeline — we need a final price before Aug 22 to route to finance.
[07:39] Samira: Understood. We'll aim to have the pricing scenarios and amendment draft by Aug 18.
[07:44] Noah: For the pilot, what metrics will Redwood provide? CPU/GPU utilization, per-request latency, token cost breakdown?
[07:52] Ethan: Yes. We'll give per-token cost, token breakdowns by prompt/response, latency p50/p95/p99, GPU utilization, cache hit rates, and model quality regression analysis vs the reference prompt set you provide.
[08:06] Maya: Can you correlate regressions to model or prompt changes? We had an incident last quarter where a model tweak altered hallucination rate.
[08:14] Ethan: We store evals and can tie quality alerts to prompt sets. Redwood Optimize gives suggestions on quant and model variant if regressions appear. We'll show a short demo in the follow-up if you'd like.
[08:27] Aaron: Yes please.
[08:29] Samira: Quick pause — anyone have other must-have deal breakers?
[08:33] Lena: Termination for cause tied to repeated SLO misses; need escalation path and right to audit.
[08:39] Priya: We'll include an escalation matrix and audit windows.
[08:42] Noah: We want a staging window where we can shift 10% traffic to EU cluster for a week before full cutover.
[08:49] Ethan: That aligns with our canary rollout features. We'll document the exact routing policy for the pilot.
[08:55] Maya: Operationally, will we still use our existing API keys or migrate to dedicated tokens for EU?
[09:01] Samira: You can keep the same API integration; we recommend route-level tokens for finer RBAC and to partition costs.
[09:08] Aaron: Ok.
[09:10] Samira: I'm going to read back the major pillars then confirm next steps. But Ethan, can you summarize the technical reqs we need from Harborlight?
[09:18] Ethan: Sure — 1) scrubbed 24h request trace with spike windows; 2) expected qps per route and peak windows; 3) HSM/K M S details if you require HSM; 4) network firewall egress rules for co-lo or onprem; 5) an infra point of contact for provisioning. Noah and Maya ok?
[09:34] Noah: Yes we'll get that.
[09:36] Maya: We'll assemble those by Aug 19.
[09:40] Samira: Great. From Redwood ops, we'll send: 1) pricing scenarios for co-lo vs onprem + staged commit pricing; 2) amendment draft w/ SLOs and EU addendum; 3) benchmark plan and expected artifacts; 4) security artifact pack (SOC2, ISO, audit log samples).
[09:55] Priya: I'll own the security artifact pack.
[09:58] Aaron: Who will be our Redwood point for day-to-day provisioning questions?
[10:02] Samira: Ethan will be primary SE, Jared will be backup for provisioning, Priya for security and contract ops, and I'll manage commercial.
[10:10] Aaron: Fine.
[10:12] [11:00] — mid-call, people checking screens, slight crosstalk —
[11:12] Maya: Quick tangent — about model variants: we want to keep the same model family but test a smaller quant variant for EU to save memory. Any risk to accuracy?
[11:22] Ethan: There's a small tradeoff. For many QA and retrieval-augmented flows quantized variants maintain parity, but for long-context summarization there can be slight degradation. We'll include accuracy delta in the bench results.
[11:36] Maya: Ok good.
[11:39] Samira: Quick note on billing — we'll produce a blended invoice option for EU cluster usage, or you can bill EU separately under a different account for data residency if that simplifies compliance.
[11:49] Aaron: Preference is to keep billing consolidated. Finance wants single invoice.
[11:53] Samira: Noted.
[11:54] Lena: Any audit trail for changes to billing rate? We need versioned contract artifacts.
[11:59] Samira: We'll provide versioned amendment documents in the deal folder and confirm via DocuSign.
[12:06] Aaron: How do we handle model updates with the private EU cluster — do you push model binaries or do we pull from an image?
[12:13] Jared: For onprem we can support a customer-controlled image pull with signed manifests. For managed co-lo we push via signed artifacts with your acceptance window.
[12:22] Noah: Good. We prefer pull-from internal registry for prod.
[12:25] Jared: Ok we'll put that in the deployment plan.
[12:28] Samira: Two other quick items — 1) backup failover path: if EU cluster is down we failover to EU-hosted region, not US, to keep latency low; 2) monitoring hooks: we'll add a SLO dashboard and incident webhook into your PagerDuty.
[12:43] Maya: PagerDuty integration is must-have.
[12:45] Priya: We'll request the PD integration info in follow-up.
[12:48] Aaron: Any showstopper on our side? I think the biggest gating item is legal review of the amendment and finance sign-off on pricing.
[12:57] Samira: Agreed. We'll target Aug 18 for pricing and amendment draft so you can circulate to legal and finance.
[13:05] Aaron: If we get the pricing on Aug 18 we can route through procurement and aim to sign by Sep 2.
[13:11] Samira: Perfect.
[13:13] [41:00] — later in call, wrap up —
[41:05] Samira: I'm going to close with a recap: 1) Redwood sends pricing scenarios (co-lo vs onprem) and an amendment draft by Aug 18; 2) Harborlight shares scrubbed 24h trace + qps + HSM details by Aug 19; 3) Redwood runs benchmark and returns results in 3–4 business days; 4) Priya sets security review for week of Aug 25. Any additions?
[41:30] Lena: Please add escalation matrix and right to audit in amendment.
[41:34] Priya: Will do.
[41:36] Aaron: Add note: 10% traffic canary for one week before cutover.
[41:41] Ethan: Noted.
[41:43] Samira: Thanks everyone. We'll send meeting notes and action items.
[41:47] Maya: Thanks.
[41:49] Noah: Thanks all.
[41:51] Samira: Ok bye.

End summary (auto):
